subject: Re: Request for regional egress paths, proxy peering and private-hosting evidence
messages:
From: Alicia Ramirez <alicia.ramirez@medicorp.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: sara.lee@medicorp.com, procurement@medicorp.com
Date: 2027-03-17T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: regional egress paths + private-proxy peering evidence for EU pilot

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the productive call this morning. As we scope the EU pilot, InfoSec needs a compact evidence bundle that demonstrates how traffic from our tenants would be scoped to EU-only egress and which controls prevent accidental cross-region egress. Specifically we need: 

- A network diagram that shows VPC peering / PrivateLink (or equivalent) endpoints and any proxy/bastion hops for EU-hosted workloads.
- Proof that KV/KMS keys for EU tenants are partitioned (snapshot of key policy or exportable report is ok).
- A short explanation of fallback routing: if a dedicated EU node is full, what automated fallback behavior occurs and where data transits. 
- Any SOC 2 control references or CAIQ assertions relevant to region-bound routing.

Target timeline: we need the bundle by EOD Thu 2027-03-20 to proceed with our legal/compliance review next week.

Attachments we expect are fine as PDFs or diagrams. If some info is sensitive, a redacted PDF with a supporting runbook link is acceptable.

Appreciate it,
Alicia
Alicia Ramirez
Lead Information Security
MediCorp Health Systems

--
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramirez <alicia.ramirez@medicorp.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, procurement@medicorp.com
Date: 2027-03-17T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: regional egress paths + private-proxy peering evidence for EU pilot

Hi Alicia,

Thanks — we can get that over. High level: Redwood supports EU-only serving for pinned tenants via private deployments or VPC peering to our EU Dedicated pools. When a tenant is pinned to EU: requests are routed into the EU pool; KV cache and KMS key material for that tenant remain in the EU region.

Im looping in David (infra) and Irene (compliance) to attach the diagram, SOC 2 references and the KMS snapshot. Expect a bundled PDF and a short runbook link by end-of-day Thursday as requested. If there are any very specific items (e.g., full CIDR egress lists or corporate peering IPs) let me know and well include them in a redacted appendix.

Next steps: 1) David will provide the VPC/private-proxy diagram and fallback routing behavior; 2) Irene will include the CAIQ/SOC2 control pointers and a brief note on audit logs retention for EU tenants; 3) Ill package attachments and send a single consolidated packet.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security Ops
Redwood Inference

--
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Ramirez <alicia.ramirez@medicorp.com>, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-18T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: VPC diagram + fallback routing details (for MediCorp)

Grace / Alicia / Irene,

Attaching the requested artifacts. Summary below and details in the attached 'redwood_vpc_diagram_v2.pdf' and runbook link: https://hippo.redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-egress-2027-03

Summary: 
- EU Dedicated pool: customer traffic that is pinned to EU terminates on EU GPU nodes in eu-west-1. PrivateLink endpoints (customer VPC <-> Redwood private endpoint) are established inside that region.
- Data plane: API requests remain in-region; prefix/KV caches are colocated with EU compute. KMS keys: we maintain customer-specific key metadata and can partition key usage by region. See 'kms_partition_snapshot.csv' for an exportable statement showing EU keys scoped.
- Fallback rules: if EU pool capacity is exhausted the routing policy is configurable per-customer. For MediCorp pilot you requested "no cross-region fallback" — we can enforce strict isolation (requests queue / 429) rather than failover to non-EU pools. The routing decision is done at the control plane and recorded in the audit stream (SOC2 CC-9/10 refs included in the PDF).
- Bastion/proxy hops: our managed private-proxy (for telemetry and debugging) is always deployed inside the same region for pinned tenants. For debug sessions that require operator access we use ephemeral bastions with time-limited certs; those sessions and IPs are logged and exported to the compliance audit stream.

Attachments included: redwood_vpc_diagram_v2.pdf (diagram), kms_partition_snapshot.csv (key mapping export), soc2_summary.pdf (control references).

If Alicia needs explicit CIDR egress ranges for firewall allowlists, say so and Ill produce a redacted list that omits internal operator addresses.

-David
David Kim
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

--
From: Alicia Ramirez <alicia.ramirez@medicorp.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medicorp.com, sara.lee@medicorp.com
Date: 2027-03-20T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: regional egress paths + private-proxy peering evidence for EU pilot

Grace / David / Irene,

Received the packet — thanks for the clear diagram and the explicit note that fallback can be set to 'no cross-region failover.' The KMS snapshot and SOC 2 references look sufficient for our preliminary review. A couple of clarifying items before procurement signs off: 

- Please provide the redacted CIDR allowlist for the EU endpoints so our network team can prepare peering ACLs (redact operator-only ranges).
- Confirm retention window for routing/audit logs for EU tenants (we require 12 months immutable export).

If you can send those two items by EOD Tuesday were on track to finalize the SOW. Procurement is looped here for the SOW timeline.

Thanks,
Alicia
